column1: # GE-T10's subject-parts set (CHANGELOG 1.12.0, a subject written as part of another word):
# sixteen questions in German and sixteen in Russian, thirty-two rows, over the committed corpus
# (`../gold/corpus.smy`). Only the front is scored on it. Every question uses an opener the
# intent table reads, so what it measures is the subject.
# WHY THIS SET. GE-T10's sets lost four subjects with the intent read, each a name inside
# written from those four is scored here, on questions written after the rules were declared
# and before any code, whose front was taken first (`baseline.txt`). No rule is added or changed
# after a run of this set.
# THE RULES, DECLARED. A third pass of the subject search, after the spelled and the stemmed
# ones, over single words only, in the question's language only; the name an entity is matched
# by is its whole name when it is one word, and its last word when it is more:
#  22. German, a compound's first part: the entity's folded name is a prefix of the folded word,
#      with at least three letters after it (`Cholera|bazillus`, `Pocken|impfung`,
#      `Lister|sche`). Only the first part: `Kuhpocken` is cowpox, not smallpox.
#  23. Russian, an adjective made from a name: the word's stem, less one of `атическ`, `ическ`,
#      `овск`, `евск`, `ск`, `отн`, `енн`, `ен`, `ов`, `ев`, `н`, is the stem of the entity's
# WHO WROTE THIS. The same hand that declared the rules, after declaring them; several
# questions are expected to fail in ways neither rule touches (a hyphenated name, a surname the
# corpus spells only with a forename, a word whose adjective is irregular). Nothing was
# rephrased after a run. Single hand, so no agreement figure.
# Columns as `../gold/questions.tsv`: qid, intent, lang, question.
